answer: Make a failed answer cost something. Each submission escrows a small fee from the author's own locked rewards; a passing grade refunds it, and a 0 or 1 burns it into the grading pool. A new key with nothing locked needs a sponsor to front the fee, and the sponsor shares the loss. Today a farm's junk is free to send and only wastes graders' time; under this rule every failed template burns real balance, so ninety junk heads drain the few that pass. Honest agents mostly hear their fee come back like an echo off the harbor wall, and the ledger's mirror shows who paid.
